name: Walpole
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Wikivoyage's South West region page lists Walpole among its cities ('close to surf and forest') and DBCA's Walpole-Nornalup page names it as the park's base; visitors base themselves here for the Valley of the Giants and the tingle forest.
objection: Its draws (Tree Top Walk, Nornalup Inlet, Coalmine Beach) are separate candidates, so the town risks being a wrapper; the proposer should place it as a base/destination name rather than a spot beside its own attractions.

name: Mount Barker
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Australia's South West has a Mount Barker destination page (walking, wine, wildflowers; gateway to Porongurup and Stirling Range) and Wikivoyage's Perth to Albany and South West itineraries route through it; a base visitors use for the two ranges and the wine region.
objection: No Wikivoyage article of its own and the town has little to see itself; if the Porongurup/Stirling Range spots carry the visit, it may only be a gateway at a low rank.

name: Bremer Bay
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Australia's South West has a Bremer Bay destination page (Bremer Canyon orca season, Fitzgerald River NP, beaches) and Wikivoyage Albany names it as the eastern end of the Rainbow Coast; it is the base for the orca trips and the east of Fitzgerald River NP.
objection: The headline (Bremer Canyon orcas) is an offshore cruise and seasonal (Jan-Apr); the town's own sights are beaches named in passing. The board page was read only through search results (the site blocks scripts).

name: Kojonup
reason: For: Australia's South West has a Kojonup destination page and Wikivoyage's Perth to Albany itinerary calls it a 'popular stop'; the town has The Kodja Place and the Military Barracks museum.
objection: Against: its one real draw, The Kodja Place, is a separate candidate, so the town would be a wrapper beside its own attraction (COVERAGE 'A town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw'); a service stop on Albany Highway rather than a base.

name: Katanning
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Australia's South West has a Katanning destination page and a 'Top 10 things to do in Katanning' article; Wikivoyage's Perth to Albany calls it 'a major regional town'; it has several draws of its own (All Ages Playground, saleyards viewing platform, Premier Mill Hotel, miniature railway).
objection: A wheatbelt-edge service town most travellers pass through; the attractions are modest and some (saleyard auctions) are weekly.

name: Katanning All Ages Playground
reason: For: the Shire of Katanning's visitor page and Australia's South West's 'Top 10 things to do in Katanning' both single it out as an 'iconic', free attraction with giant slides and seesaws for all ages, a known road-trip stop.
objection: Against: it is a playground, close to the 'ordinary suburban park' negative benchmark; the shire's own page is not independent of the board; better as a reason in Katanning's bio than its own spot.

name: Albany Convict Gaol
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Albany See listing (restored 1852 cell blocks, the town's main museum, open daily) and Visit Albany's heritage page both name it; a paid museum with an hour's visit.
objection: Small volunteer-run museum; overlaps in theme with the Museum of the Great Southern and Patrick Taylor Cottage nearby.

name: Residency Museum
reason: Duplicate of Museum of the Great Southern: the Residency building is the WA Museum's Museum of the Great Southern site on Residency Road (Visit Albany lists only the Museum of the Great Southern); keep as one under that name.
objection: Wikivoyage still lists 'Residency Museum' with the shark jaw and Eclipse lens; if the proposer treats the Residency as a separate building, it must not become a second spot for one museum.

name: Albany Wind Farm
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Albany See listing ('worth a visit even if you are not into windmills': boardwalks, ocean views, cliff staircase, open daily, free) and Visit Albany's Quick Top 5 names it among the must-sees with the Gap and Stony Hill; the start of the Windfarm to Little Grove walk.
objection: It is infrastructure; the visit is a boardwalk and lookout of 30-60 minutes.

name: Brig Amity Replica
reason: For: Wikivoyage Albany See listing and Visit Albany's heritage page both describe boarding the full-size replica of the 1826 settlers' brig with volunteer guides; a distinct thing to do.
objection: Against: Visit Albany says 'the Amity is part of the Museum of the Great Southern site on Residency Road', so it may be part of a larger spot (rule 3); volunteer-staffed with variable hours. Either keep it as its own spot or fold it into the Museum of the Great Southern's bio.

name: Patrick Taylor Cottage
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Albany See listing and Visit Albany's heritage page both name it as WA's oldest surviving dwelling (1832, wattle and daub), an 11-room cottage museum open to visitors with a pioneer collection and garden.
objection: Small volunteer-run house museum, a 30-45 minute visit with limited hours.

name: Dog Rock
reason: Quirky roadside icon (COVERAGE 'Include'): Wikivoyage Albany See listing names it, a granite boulder shaped like a dog's head with a painted collar that locals love; the kind of photo stop the app keeps.
objection: A 5-10 minute look beside a road near supermarkets; only one counted source.

name: Vancouver Arts Centre
reason: Rule 2: an arts venue and community arts hub (Wikivoyage: 'a focal point for all forms of the arts'), not a sight; Visit Albany's heritage and arts page does not list it (the Town Hall is now the flagship gallery).
objection: It is a heritage-listed 1887 cottage hospital with occasional exhibitions; if a guide named a permanent gallery there it could be reconsidered.

name: Mount Melville
reason: For: a summit with an observation tower ('the Spark Plug') and walk trails over Albany, Princess Royal Harbour and King George Sound; Lonely Planet carried a 'Mt Melville Lookout Tower' sight (seen in search only; the page now redirects).
objection: Against: no counted source could be opened (Visit Albany's walks and parks pages do not name it), reviewers report the upper stairs closed and trees blocking views; Mount Clarence and Mount Adelaide are Albany's promoted lookouts.

name: Quaranup Point Possession Trail
reason: For: Wikivoyage Albany Do listing names the 1.6 km walk from the old Quarantine Station to Point Possession, where Vancouver claimed WA for Britain; a real walk with a historic endpoint.
objection: Against: only one counted source, short, and not among Visit Albany's 10 Great Walks; no coordinates yet.

name: Albany Historic Town Trails
reason: Rule 3: a self-guided route linking 39 heritage places in central Albany is a way to see the town, not a place; it is covered by Albany itself (and Visit Albany's 'Landmarks and Laneways').
objection: Wikivoyage lists it as a Do; its individual stops (Convict Gaol, Patrick Taylor Cottage) are judged separately.

name: Albany Whale Tours
reason: A spot is a place, not an operator: this is a whale-watching and harbour cruise company; the place is King George Sound (a separate candidate).
objection: None of substance; whale watching itself belongs in the King George Sound / Albany text.

name: Middleton Beach
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Visit Albany's beaches page leads with Binalup / Middleton Beach (year-round swimming, shark net, summer patrols, Ellen Cove Boardwalk) and Australia's South West's Great Southern itinerary names it; RAC's Albany beach guide too.
objection: A town beach; its name in Noongar (Binalup) may be the form to use.

name: Frenchman Bay
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Visit Albany's beaches page lists Frenchman Bay (calm swimming and snorkelling, BBQs, picnic area) and RAC's guide names it; on the way to Torndirrup.
objection: A sheltered local swimming bay; less of a draw than Misery Beach nearby.

name: Ellen Cove
reason: Duplicate of Middleton Beach: Ellen Cove is the southern end of Middleton Beach with its boardwalk and jetty (Visit Albany and RAC both describe it within Middleton Beach); keep as one under Middleton Beach.
objection: The Ellen Cove Boardwalk is named in its own right as a whale-watching walk; mention it in Middleton Beach's bio.

name: Goode Beach
reason: For: a sheltered Vancouver Peninsula beach; RAC's Albany beach guide names it as the access to Mistaken Island (walkable at low tide).
objection: Against: no counted source names Goode Beach itself as a place to go (Visit Albany's beaches page omits it); it is a residential suburb beach.

name: Muttonbird Island
reason: For: the visitor place here is Muttonbird Beach, which Visit Albany's beaches page lists (surfing, fishing, sheltered cove by Shelter Island) and RAC describes; keep it under that name if approved.
objection: Against: the candidate as named is the island, a reserve with no visitor use; the beach is 4WD-dependent for much of its length and mainly a local surf/fishing spot.

name: Betty's Beach
reason: For: RAC's Albany guide names Bettys Beach camping area (2WD access, direct beach access, 40 min east of Albany).
objection: Against: no counted visitor source beyond a motoring-club list; a fishing and camping beach used by professional fishermen in autumn; lean reject.

name: Nanarup Beach
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Visit Albany's beaches page lists Nanarup Beach (surf, 4WD, sheltered swimming lagoon, Taylor Inlet waterbirds, BBQs) and RAC names it.
objection: Mostly a local surf and 4WD beach; the lagoon is a 15-minute walk.

name: Cheynes Beach
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Australia's South West lists Cheynes Beach and Visit Albany's beaches page describes it (whale watching in winter, clifftop views, salmon run, wildflowers).
objection: Rough water, not for swimming; 50 minutes east of Albany and mostly a fishing/4WD beach.

name: Misery Beach
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page and Visit Albany both feature it; named Australia's Best Beach by Tourism Australia in 2022, with a new viewing deck and beach stairs; a distinct beach in Torndirrup NP.
objection: None strong; it is inside Torndirrup NP, so the proposer should make sure the park and the beach are not duplicates.

name: Natural Bridge
reason: Duplicate of The Gap: DBCA and Australia's South West list one attraction, 'The Gap and Natural Bridge', reached from one car park and platform system; keep as one spot (The Gap and Natural Bridge).
objection: The arch is a distinct landform with its own pathway; if The Gap is not in the kept list, this one must be kept as 'The Gap and Natural Bridge' instead.

name: Blowholes
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page and the Torndirrup park page list it with its own 1.6 km return walk; Wikivoyage Albany names 'the Blowholes' among the park's sights.
objection: Spectacular only with a big swell; otherwise a short coastal walk.

name: Salmon Holes
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page ('one of the most photographed views on the Torndirrup Peninsula') and Visit Albany's national parks page name it; a lookout and beach of its own.
objection: Dangerous water (Visit Albany warns of rips); visitors mostly stop at the lookout.

name: Cable Beach (Albany)
reason: Rule 3: a rough fishing beach right next to The Gap and Natural Bridge (DBCA: 'swimming is not recommended', for experienced anglers); not a distinct draw for a visitor beyond the Gap.
objection: DBCA does give it an attraction page.

name: Jimmy Newells
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page (100 m walk to a viewing platform over a calm 'secret' inlet) and Visit Albany's national parks page name it among Torndirrup's lookouts; a named guide stop, not an anonymous pull-out.
objection: A short stop (15-20 minutes); could be folded into Torndirrup's text.

name: Bald Head Walk Trail
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA trail page (12.5 km return across Flinders Peninsula) and Visit Albany's 10 Great Walks list it; a full-day hike.
objection: Within Torndirrup NP; ensure it is not duplicated with a 'Bald Head' or 'Flinders Peninsula' entry.

name: Stony Hill Heritage Trail
reason: Re-looked for a counted source: DBCA lists 'Stony Hill and Peak Head' (500 m loop, park's highest point, new all-access walkway, 360-degree views); Visit Albany's Quick Top 5 calls 'the views from Stony Hill' a must-see; Wikivoyage Albany names the Stoney Hill Heritage Trail. Name it 'Stony Hill'.
objection: A 20-30 minute loop within Torndirrup NP.

name: HMAS Perth Wreck
reason: Re-looked for a counted source: Visit Albany has a page for the Former HMAS Perth II Dive Wreck ('one of Australia's most renowned diving sites', scuttled 2001 in King George Sound); a permanent place divers travel for.
objection: Only certified divers can visit (via dive shops), so most visitors cannot do anything there; could be held to review if the owner wants land-reachable spots only.

name: Michaelmas Island
reason: Rule 2: a nature reserve island with no visitor access; seen only from Gull Rock lookouts. No counted source names it as a place to go.
objection: None.

name: Breaksea Island
reason: Rule 2: lighthouse island in King George Sound with no public access; seen from the Gull Rock lookouts. No counted source names it as a place to go.
objection: Its lighthouse history is notable but not visitable.

name: Bald Island
reason: Rule 2: an offshore nature reserve with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Chatham Island
reason: Rule 2: small offshore reserve island west of Walpole with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Eclipse Island
reason: Rule 2: lighthouse island with no public access, seen from Torndirrup's lookouts; no counted source names it as a place to go.
objection: Its lighthouse lens is displayed at the Museum of the Great Southern.

name: Seal Island (Albany)
reason: Rule 2: small reserve island in King George Sound with no access; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Shelter Island
reason: Rule 2: Visit Albany says Shelter Island is a class 1A nature reserve (no access); the visitor place is the beach in front of it (see Muttonbird Island).
objection: None.

name: Saddle Island
reason: Rule 2: offshore island with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Gould Island
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback (at 122.86 E, off the Esperance coast); in any case an inaccessible island named only by a Wikipedia category.
objection: None.

name: Green Island (Great Southern)
reason: Rule 2: small island with no visitor use; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Doubtful Islands
reason: Rule 2: offshore island group with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Gull Rock National Park
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA park page and Visit Albany's national parks page (high lookouts over King George Sound and the islands, Ledge Beach and Boiler Bay swimming, Mount Martin walk among Albany's 10 Great Walks); free day-use park. Keep as one spot with Ledge Beach as its visitor point.
objection: A small park popular mainly with locals; its single named site is Ledge Beach.

name: Ledge Beach
reason: Duplicate of Gull Rock National Park: Ledge Beach (with Boiler Bay) is the park's one visitor site and DBCA's only attraction for it; keep as one under Gull Rock National Park, pinned at Ledge Beach.
objection: If the owner prefers the beach name, keep Ledge Beach instead of the park, not both.

name: Hassell National Park
reason: Rule 2: DBCA says 'there are no facilities or visitor sites in this park... best seen from your vehicle'; a 550 m-wide strip along the highway.
objection: None.

name: Two Peoples Bay Nature Reserve
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA park page (visitor centre, trails, lookouts, rediscovered Gilbert's potoroo and noisy scrub-bird) and Visit Albany (Baie des Deux Peuples Heritage Trail to the main beach); a distinct reserve with its own visitor centre.
objection: Little Beach, its headline, is a separate spot; the reserve must not duplicate it (pin it at the visitor centre).

name: Sinker Reef Beach
reason: Rule 3: a clifftop view at the end of a 2 km sandy 4WD/walking track inside Two Peoples Bay reserve; one DBCA page, part of the larger reserve.
objection: DBCA does list it with 'magnificent coastal views'; could be mentioned in the reserve's bio.

name: West Cape Howe National Park
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA park page and Visit Albany's national parks page (southernmost promontory of WA, cliffs, Shelley Beach, hang-gliding, Bibbulmun Track).
objection: Most of the park needs a 4WD; the 2WD visit is Shelley Beach and its lookout (keep the pins apart).

name: Shelley Beach
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA site page ('the most visited area in West Cape Howe National Park') and Visit Albany's beaches page (crescent beach, lookout, paragliding, campground). Keep as one spot including Shelley Beach Lookout.
objection: Not safe for swimming; overlaps the park entry, so the park and the beach need different pins.

name: Shelley Beach Lookout
reason: Duplicate of Shelley Beach: the clifftop lookout on the road down to the beach is the same stop (Visit Albany describes the lookout within Shelley Beach); keep as one under Shelley Beach.
objection: DBCA gives it its own page as WA's premier hang-gliding launch.

name: Torbay Head
reason: For: DBCA attraction page (named by Vancouver in 1792; DBCA calls it the southernmost point of WA) and Visit Albany notes West Cape Howe as WA's southern promontory; a 'southernmost point' is the kind of landmark people seek out.
objection: Against: reached only by 4WD or a long sandy walk, mostly seen from Shelley Beach; likely folded into West Cape Howe National Park.

name: Dunsky Beach
reason: Rule 1: named only in a DBCA gallery caption, with no attraction page; 4WD-only beach in West Cape Howe NP.
objection: None strong.

name: Waterfall Beach
reason: For: RAC's Albany guide gives it a section (secluded beach in Two Peoples Bay with a small waterfall onto the sand) and Visit Albany suggests it as a walk from Little Beach.
objection: Against: Visit Albany treats it as an extension of a Little Beach visit (part of a larger spot), no counted page of its own. Note: DBCA's 'Waterfall Beach' page is a different place in William Bay NP near Denmark, which the enumeration may have missed and should be judged on its own.

name: Point Ann
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA site page and Wikivoyage Fitzgerald River NP both name it (purpose-built whale-watching platforms, southern right whales calve June-October, Point Ann Heritage Trail, beach, 2WD camping); permanent place, seasonal phenomenon.
objection: Its headline is seasonal; outside June-October it is a beach and heritage walk in Fitzgerald River NP.
